subcategory: post-retrieval temporal alignment filtering for fuzzy time expressions
task: Time-sensitive question answering / retrieval with fuzzy temporal expressions
problem: Dense retrievers rank by semantic similarity and return topically relevant but temporally misaligned documents, especially when queries or documents use vague expressions such as 'a few years later'.
architecture: DeFuzzRAG: (1) a small LM extracts the query's temporal intent as a structured interval; (2) query-aware temporal metadata are generated on the fly for the top-K retrieved documents; (3) temporal alignment filtering re-ranks or discards inconsistent passages; no retriever or generator retraining. Also introduces the Time Attention Ratio (TAR) diagnostic.
retriever: MPNet (top-5) with FAISS; compared with BM25, Contriever, BGE
generator: GPT-3.5; temporal parser SLMs LLaMA-2-7B, Mistral-7B, OpenChat-3.5, TinyLLaMA-1.1B (GPT-4 reference)
llm_or_encoder: MPNet retriever; 7B SLM parser; GPT-3.5 generator

datasets.name: TempFuzz-QA
datasets.details: benchmark of fuzzified temporal queries (explicit vs fuzzified versions)

key_results: Hit Rate improves by 15.7% over standard RAG on TempFuzz-QA and TAR rises by 27.7% on average.
Fuzzified-query HR 0.7765 (LLaMA2-7B parser) vs 0.6712 for MPNet and 0.7426 for BGE.
Mistral-7B parser reaches MRR 0.5402 vs 0.5483 for GPT-4 at much lower latency (2.84 vs 11.14 s per query).
strengths: Plug-and-play, training-free and model-agnostic; works on top of unmodified retrievers.
Analyses performance by fuzziness type and query type.

limitations.text: Spatial-fuzziness evaluation is only a preliminary demonstration.
Generalized dating expressions (broad or seasonal) remain hardest; small parsers such as TinyLLaMA-1.1B lose MRR (0.4702).
Evaluation centres on retrieval metrics on a self-built benchmark; end-to-end answer quality is not the main reported outcome.

notes: Adds 1-3 s latency per query depending on the parser.
title: DeFuzzRAG: Handling Fuzzy Time Expressions for Temporal Robustness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
